records.stage: developing CNS and adult brain (as printed: 'developing CNS ... also for the adult brain')
records.methods: Terminology revision by the FIPAT Working Group Neuroanatomy (Terminologia Neuroanatomica, TNA); stored Wiley passage plus complete PubMed abstract read. No full text.

findings.statement: The TNA defines the rostral border of D1 at the rostral border of the chiasmatic plate and names the part rostral to D1 'Telencephalon medium' (T); D1 and T roughly correspond to the secondary prosencephalon.
findings.support: The rostral border of D1 was defined as the rostral border of the chiasmatic plate, so as to include the eye vesicle in D1, and T (Telencephalon medium) as the part rostral to D1.

findings.statement: The TNA adopts the prosomeric model of Puelles and Rubinstein (neuromere-based) as the organising framework for terminology of the developing CNS and also the adult brain.
findings.support: In the revised version of the TE and in the TNA, the prosomeric model developed by Luis Puelles and John Rubinstein ... was adopted.

records.terminology: Telencephalon medium (T) = part rostral to D1 (rostral border of the chiasmatic plate); D1 + T roughly = secondary prosencephalon; prosomeric/neuromeric framework adopted. The paraphysis is not named in the text read.
records.caveats: Only the stored Wiley passage and the abstract were read; the paraphysis is not mentioned in either, so nothing about its terminological placement is stated here. The passage is a fragment, so the full TNA treatment of the telencephalon medium (and any entry for the paraphysis) could not be checked. Acronyms TE/D1 are used as printed without expansion.

appraisal.note: Terminology proposal (FIPAT/IFAA consensus), not an observational study; no paraphysis claim to appraise; only a passage and the abstract were read.

records.stage: tissue samples; colloid cyst cases mean age 46.7 years (as printed)
records.methods: Immunohistochemistry for PAX8 (C-terminus specific antibody), TTF1, SOX17 and cadherin 17 on 15 colloid cysts, 7 Rathke cleft cysts, 8 neurenteric cysts and 10 craniopharyngiomas; extent and intensity scored.

findings.statement: All 15 third-ventricle colloid cysts were PAX8 positive (moderate to strong in >50% of cells in 13/15), whereas no Rathke cleft cyst, neurenteric cyst or craniopharyngioma was PAX8 positive.
findings.support: All 15 cases of CCs were PAX8 positive (moderate to strong expression in >50 % in 13/15 cases), while no RCC, NEC or craniopharyngioma showed PAX8 immunoreactivity.

findings.statement: No TTF1 or SOX17 expression and only weak scattered cadherin 17; authors conclude colloid cysts lack signs of thyroid, mullerian or enteric differentiation (a comparator for colloid-cyst histogenesis).
findings.support: Colloid cysts of the 3rd ventricle are consistently PAX8-positive, while they lack signs of thyroid, müllerian or enteric differentiation.

findings.statement: Rare PAX8-positive single cells were seen in 3 of 6 choroid plexus samples examined.
findings.support: Rare PAX8-positive cells were also observed in single cells of 50 % (3/6) of the choroid plexuses.

records.terminology: Colloid cyst of the 3rd ventricle described as a 'cystic lesion of uncertain histogenesis, occurring exclusively in the 3rd ventricle close to the foramen Monro'. The paraphysis is not mentioned in the abstract.

records.methods: Short note (pp. 128-129); only the stored Wiley passage was read. Descriptive comparison of the dorsal sack across taxa; methods not stated.

findings.statement: The dorsal sack is defined as a pouchlike evagination of the diatela, located between the epiphysis and the paraphysis, in many lower vertebrates.
findings.support: In many of the lower vertebrates there is a pouchlike evagination of the diatela (membranous roof of the diacele, or "third ventricle") between the epiphysis and the paraphysis.

findings.statement: Dorsal sack form varies by taxon: anteverted and very large in Ceratodus and Polyodon, projecting dorsad in the green turtle, crowded caudad by the cerebrum onto the retroverted epiphysis in mammals.
findings.support: In the green turtle it projects dorsad. Its mammalian representative is crowded caudad by the cerebrum and rests upon the retroverted epiphysis.

findings.statement: The diaplexuses (choroid plexuses of the diatela) are continued into the dorsal sack; the sack is large in the sheep and long in the cow and horse.
findings.support: It is large in the sheep and long in the cow and horse. The diaplexuses are continued into it.

records.terminology: Uses 'dorsal sack' for a pouch of the diatela (membranous roof of the diacele, or 'third ventricle') between epiphysis and paraphysis; 'diaplexuses' for the plexuses of the diatela; the author says he figured it earlier without recognizing its homology. The paraphysis is mentioned only as the rostral landmark.

mentions.quote: It is commonly ignored in figures and descriptions, but was shown by Reichert.

mentions.claim: The speaker figured the structure there without recognizing its homology.
mentions.quote: The speaker, without recognizing its homology, figured it in the *New York Medical Journal*, 1885, p. 320.

records.caveats: Only a short Wiley excerpt was read (a brief note, probably a society communication; not confirmed). Publication year is not in the text read (Wiley date field is implausible per finder notes). 'diacele' and 'diatela' are the source's terms.
